title: prefetchable shared-reservation allocator with hysteresis-driven slab reclaimer
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: High-concurrency continuous-batching workloads expose two related sources of tail-latency and throughput loss in the paged KV cache: (1) contention and fragmentation in the block allocator when many small requests allocate and release slots concurrently, and (2) reactive prefetching that either overfetches cold blocks or stalls hot-path allocations while waiting on reclamation. Motivation: Reduce allocator lock contention, improve reuse of hot blocks across tenants, and ensure prefetching does not induce stalls. This PR implements a prefetchable shared-reservation allocator combined with a hysteresis-driven slab reclaimer and tenant-aware reservation hints. Summary of changes: - Introduce SharedReservation token: callers can acquire a lightweight reservation token that guarantees a best-effort slot will be available for the next N allocations. The token abstracts a reservation window to allow callers to prefetch or warm KV ranges without immediate blocking. - Prefetchable allocator path: new fast-path in block_allocator that consumes SharedReservation tokens; when a token is present the allocator will attempt to allocate from a reserved mini-pool before taking global locks. This reduces cross-core contention during continuous-batching. - Hysteresis slab reclaimer: slab_reclaimer now uses dual-threshold hysteresis per-slab (low/high watermarks) to avoid thundering reclaims under oscillating load; background reclaims are rate-limited and may defer to on-path eviction when latency SLO allows. - Tenant-aware reservation hints: scheduler exposes tenant access patterns to allocator via a small hints API so the allocator can bias reservations to tenants with tight latency budgets. - Kernel selection hint plumbing: added a small opt-in hint so the serving runtime can prefer quantized kernels when allocation pressure is high to reduce memory footprint and speed eviction. - Metrics and tracing: new metrics for reservation token usage, reservation miss rate, prefetch hit rate, and hysteresis-triggered reclaim counts. Added traces on allocation hot-path for post-mortem analysis. - Tests & benchmarks: unit tests for SharedReservation semantics, stress test to reproduce prior contention, and end-to-end benchmarks showing improvements in 99th percentile latency under continuous batching. Commits (high-level): - commit 1: add SharedReservation token type, token pool, and API surface
- commit 2: implement prefetchable fast-path in block_allocator and fallback logic
- commit 3: add hysteresis-based slab_reclaimer with rate limits and metrics
- commit 4: tenant hint plumbing, kernel selection hint integration, docs and tests
- commit 5: benchmark rig, CI tuning, and minor fixes Review summary: Initial implementation accepted by reviewers after two rounds of iteration. Main reviewer concerns were correctness under failure paths (token cleanup on panic), ensuring no unbounded memory growth with reservations, and clarity around tenant hint privacy/safety. All concerns addressed: tokens are tied to request lifetimes and reconciled in allocator shutdown paths; reservation pools are capacity-limited and observable via metrics; tenant hints are opt-in per-tenant and sanitized before use. Performance: On our continuous-batching benchmark (64 clients, batch size 8, mixed read/write, seq_len=512) this change reduced allocation median time by ~38% and 99th percentile tail allocation latency by ~54% compared to baseline. End-to-end 99th percentile generation latency improved by ~22% at peak load with no regression in throughput. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated (kv.reservation_prefetch.enabled=false by default). Gradual rollout to prod: enable for canary fleet (10%) for 48h, collect reservation miss metrics and prefetch hit rate, then 50% for 72h before full rollout. Operator docs: added tuning guidance in docs/ops/kv-tuning.md describing reservation window sizing and hysteresis thresholds. Migration notes: none required for on-disk format; runtime-only behavior change. Related work: This complements the recent KV hotprefix pinning work (see ENG-3110) by focusing on allocator-level smoothing and prefetch coordination.

review_comments: Diego: Nice approach — can you explain how tokens are reclaimed if a request panics? Please add a test path.
Aisha: tokens are tied to RequestContext and we added a drop handler; added unit test that simulates panic via assert panic in test_reservation.rs.
Linnea: Hysteresis thresholds look reasonable, but we should expose them as ops tunables and document tradeoffs.
Aisha: thresholds exposed in docs and values.yaml; added examples for conservative/aggressive profiles.
Marcus: Is there any risk of starvation for lower-priority tenants when reservations are biased? Consider a fairness cap.
Aisha: added a per-tenant max-reservation cap and a metric for reservation unfairness; allocator will round-robin if cap reached.
QA: stress test reproduced old contention pattern; with feature flag enabled we see 54% drop in allocation tail latency. CI flaky on one lint rule fixed in follow-up commit.
release_notes: Add prefetchable shared-reservation allocator and hysteresis-driven slab reclaimer to reduce KV allocation contention and tail latency under continuous-batching workloads; feature gated and off by default. Recommended operators to tune reservation window and hysteresis thresholds for their workload.
files_touched_summary: Allocator: added reservation fast-path and token lifecycle; Reclaimer: hysteresis watermarks and rate limiting; Scheduler: hint plumbing; Telemetry: new reservation and prefetch metrics; Docs and benchmarks for ops guidance.
testing_summary: Unit tests for token semantics, stress tests reproducing prior contention, and end-to-end continuous-batching benchmarks. Canary rollout plan and metrics to observe reservation misses and prefetch hit rate.
notes_for_oncall: If seeing migration of memory usage or unexpected reservation growth: check kv.reservation_prefetch.enabled, reservation_miss_rate, reservation_pool_size and per-tenant caps. Feature flag can be disabled dynamically to revert to baseline allocator behavior.
